text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Some 1,000 miners at the coalmine in Comanesti went on strike to demand the resignation of the mine's general manager.
- Economic stabilisation in Romania should start with fast reforms, the paper quotes IMF mission chief Poul Thomsen as saying.
- The leu's retail price hovers around 8,000 to the dollar.
- Opinions of various ministers and top officials on the package of economic reforms presented by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea on Monday.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Prices for petrol and diesel oil rose by 50 percent.
- SNCFR railway authority plans to sell 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron.
- January foreign investments in Romania amounted to $4.1 million, the paper says.
- Bread factories will purchase wheat through tenders.
- Opinions of local politicians and businessmen on Romania's planned reforms.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's insurance sector needs a new legislation, the paper says.
- Average monthly pensions will amount to some 299,000 lei.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Implementation of the government's reform package will have devastating social effects, Teodor Melescanu, spokesman for the former ruling Party of Social Democracy is quoted as saying.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Some 3,500 jail convicts went on hunger strike at Jilava penitentiary to protest against changes to the penal code.
- The government should explain to the population why the newly proposed reforms are necessary in order to relaunch Romania's economy.
- Big trade unions are still reluctant to take a clear stand on the package of reforms presented by the government.

- Ukraine does not oppose Romania's plans to join NATO, which it sees as a move to enhance security in the region, parliament speaker Ion Diaconescu quoted a saying after a meeting with Ukrainian officials.
ADEVARUL
- Romania's exiled King Michael plans to visit Romania by end-February or early in March, the paper says.
- European Commission president Jacques Santer will visit Romania over March 6-7.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- A local survey shows that 62 percent of Bucharesters agree with the reforms set forth by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.
- Paper quotes President Emil Constantinescu as saying in interview pick-up that "NATO has no meaning without Poland or Romania".
- Theology professor Gheorghe Anghelescu was appointed head of the government's religious denominations department.
- Report on how police arrrested Syrian-born businessman Zaher Iskandarani, believed to be one of the local lords of cigarette smuggling.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- "France lacks a clear perception of what Romania really is," French ambassador to Romania Bernard Boyer says in interview. France's support to Romania's accession to NATO is "firm and final", he says.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright proposes a meeting between NATO, Russia and the candidates to early admission to the Alliance.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
